subject.title: [Feature]: Harden Control UI Lit lifecycle boundaries

question: Should the Control UI Lit lifecycle hardening land as one broad modernization slice, or be split into smaller controller/base-element PRs by lifecycle seam?
rationale: The source evidence supports the work, but the protected label and broad UI surface require maintainer intent on scope and sequencing before repair automation should act.

options.title: Split by lifecycle seam
options.body: Create separate reviewable PRs for shared host/i18n, external-source subscriptions, router pending/not-found state, and chat post-render/persistence teardown.

options.title: Land one modernization slice
options.body: Allow one larger coordinated PR if the owner wants a single refactor and it includes broad Control UI regression and browser proof.

options.title: Narrow to proven bugs only
options.body: Defer shared abstractions and only fix source-proven lifecycle races with individual tests as they become reproducible.

recommendation.title: Split by lifecycle seam
recommendation.body: Create separate reviewable PRs for shared host/i18n, external-source subscriptions, router pending/not-found state, and chat post-render/persistence teardown.

likelyOwner.reason: Shakker is the strongest current-main history signal for the implicated Control UI lifecycle files.
